summary.name: Nmap
summary.one_liner: Nmap ("Network Mapper") is a free, open source utility for network discovery and security auditing that finds hosts, services, operating systems and firewalls on a network.
use_cases: finding open ports and running services
summary.what_it_does: Nmap uses raw IP packets to determine which hosts are available on a network, what services (name and version) they offer, which operating systems they run, and what packet filters or firewalls are in use. It supports many TCP and UDP port scanning methods, OS detection, version detection and ping sweeps. The suite also includes Zenmap (a GUI and results viewer), Ncat (data transfer and debugging), Ndiff (comparing scan results) and Nping (packet generation and response analysis). It is designed to scan large networks quickly but also works on single hosts.
notable: Includes Zenmap GUI, Ncat, Ndiff and Nping alongside the command-line scanner
Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE) scripts extend scanning
Free and open source with full source code available under its license
caveats: Page says Nmap comes with no warranty; support is community-based via mailing lists and IRC
